claims.text: An active-learning, machine-learning-based multi-resolution interpolation framework can accurately reproduce solid–liquid free-energy differences at fusion conditions.
The framework can retain vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration contributions to the phase free energies.
The framework will drastically reduce computational cost relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The framework will drastically reduce computational cost relative to TOR-TILD.
Active learning can generate property- and system-specific interatomic-potential training sets from a limited amount of ab initio data.
The actively learned model can be specifically trained to capture anharmonicity and electron–vibration coupling.
Free-energy interpolation can replace exhaustive molecular-dynamics sampling.
The proposed method is applicable across elemental, binary, and multicomponent high-entropy systems near fusion.
An actively learned machine-learning interatomic potential can mediate between ab initio-level accuracy and computational efficiency.
Active learning targets critical configurational regions relevant to the phase transition.
The learned potential can interpolate solid and liquid free-energy landscapes while accounting for vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration interactions.
Targeted active-learning data generation reduces the number of costly ab initio calculations.
Predicted phase free energies and transition properties will agree with full ab initio molecular-dynamics results to within approximately 5%.
The proposed approach will be approximately an order of magnitude faster than full ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed approach will scale more efficiently than TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
Applicability may be limited when relevant configurations lie outside the actively learned training space.
Strong long-range ordering may limit the applicability of the method.
Performance may degrade at extreme compositions or temperatures where training data are sparse.
A deviation greater than 5% from ab initio molecular-dynamics benchmarks in key observables over a significant set of conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
